claim.date_text_original: Classical Athens, broadly sixth to fourth centuries BCE
claim.summary: Specialist scholarship treats slavery as integral to Classical Athenian society and economy. Slaves were embedded in household, productive, commercial and civic contexts, and Athens is regularly analyzed as a slave society rather than merely a society in which some enslaved people were present. The atlas records a strong positive slavery designation for Classical Athens while leaving demographic prevalence and sector-specific intensity unquantified and assigning no new post-M1 P-level.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy claim ae30281b-d7c3-4e89-be55-1471fa6bfa0f. Legacy P4 remains historical metadata only and is not copied into this post-M1 claim.
